translationRepairs: At the time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants. The emperor brought Shang and Dan into court as grand counselors of the household, promoted Ban Bo to chief commandant of waters and parks, and had him serve as Palace Attendant together with the two Shi men; all held the salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.

At the time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants. The emperor brought Shang and Dan into court as grand counselors of the household, promoted Ban Bo to chief commandant of waters and parks, and had him serve as Palace Attendant together with his two teachers; all held the salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
Focus unit 與兩師並侍中 follows 許商 and 師丹 as Bo's instructors; 兩師 means those two teachers, not two men surnamed Shi. The proposed idiomatic repair restores that sense without inventing content.

At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was superintendent of the household for the heir apparent; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with the two Shi men he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.

At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was superintendent of the household for the heir apparent; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with his two teachers he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
The same clause 與兩師並侍中 names Bo's two teachers Xu Shang and Shi Dan; rendering 兩師 as "the two Shi men" misreads 師 as a shared surname. The literal repair is accurate.

Only Gu Yong once said, "In the Jianhe and Heping era the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the previous court, scorched the four quarters, and their gifts had no measure; they emptied the inner treasury; favor to women reached an extreme that could not be surpassed;

Only Gu Yong once said, "In the Jianshi and Heping era the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the previous court, scorched the four quarters, and their gifts had no measure; they emptied the inner treasury; favor to women reached an extreme that could not be surpassed;
Focus unit 建始、河平之際 uses the era name 建始 (Jianshi); Jianhe would be 建和. Correcting only that era name matches the Chinese and the idiomatic already on the same unit.

Ban Biao, styled Shuipi, studied abroad with his cousin Ban Si while the household enjoyed imperial book grants and deep coffers, drawing classicists from afar so that even Yang Xuan and his father's circle beat a path to their door.

Ban Biao, styled Shuipi, studied abroad with his cousin Ban Si while the household enjoyed imperial book grants and deep coffers, drawing classicists from afar so that even Yang Xiong and his father's circle beat a path to their door.
Focus unit 父黨揚子雲以下 names Yang Xiong by courtesy name 子雲; Yang Xuan invents a different person. The proposed idiomatic replacement is correct.

Biao, courtesy name Shuipi, in youth roamed in study with his elder cousin Si; the family possessed books granted by the throne and was ample in wealth, so lovers of antiquity came from distant regions, and from Yang Xuan downward none of his father's associates failed to visit the gate.

Biao, courtesy name Shuipi, in youth roamed in study with his elder cousin Si; the family possessed books granted by the throne and was ample in wealth, so lovers of antiquity came from distant regions, and from Yang Xiong downward none of his father's associates failed to visit the gate.
The same 揚子雲 is Yang Xiong (Ziyun), not Yang Xuan. The literal repair restores the attested personal name.
Duanmu Ci's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
Duan Ganmu's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
木偃息以蕃魏兮 alludes to Duan Ganmu (段干木), whose withdrawal strengthened Wei; Duanmu Ci does not fit. The worker found the correct person, but the corpus convention writes the name as Duan Ganmu.

Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both charged as unfilial.

Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both accused of capital crimes.
The unit ends 皆不道; 不道 is a grave Han legal category, not 不孝 'unfilial.' 'Capital crimes' conveys the legal force without the worker's cumbersome gloss inside the sentence.
Wei Shou of old guarded his brother, yet the brother turned raider and ruined him.
Shu Wu once guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.

The allusion is not to a person named Wei Shu. 衛叔 abbreviates Shu Wu of Wei, who guarded the state for his elder brother, Duke Cheng; 昆 means that elder brother. The worker caught the bad reading Shou but did not resolve the historical allusion.

Think of vertical and horizontal schemers, exiled tongues, Shang Yang's triple trick on Duke Xiao, Li Si's grab at Qin's moment—they rode storm and crisis, gambled on crooked odds, blazed one dawn and burned by dusk; rogues rued it—should an honest man copy them?

Think of the vertical and horizontal strategists and the exiles who peddled their arguments: Shang Yang used three techniques to insinuate himself with Duke Xiao, and Li Si exploited the needs of the age to win over the First Emperor. They caught the winds of opportunity and rode the turmoil of their times, seizing crooked chances to gain a day's wealth and honor. Glorious in the morning, by evening they were ruined; their good fortune did not last a moment, while their calamities burdened the age. Even evil men came to regret this path. How much less should a good man rely on it?

李斯奮時務而要始皇 explicitly names the First Emperor and describes Li Si using the demands of the age to win him over. The worker found the omitted referent, but both its proposal and the prior compressed English obscured much of the passage.
Gao Yao advised Yu, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;
Gao Yao advised Shun, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;
Focus unit 咎繇謨虞 uses 虞 for Shun (有虞), not 禹 Yu the Great. Gao Yao advising Shun is the standard pairing; the repair removes the false referent.
Formerly Gao Yao counseled Yu, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;
Formerly Gao Yao counseled Shun, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;
The same 謨虞 denotes counseling Shun; rendering 虞 as Yu the Great confuses distinct graphs and persons. The literal repair is correct.
Fu Yue rose from a cliff dream, Lü Wang from the Wei shallows, Ning Qi from a roadside song, Zhang Liang from a book at dawn—they waited Heaven's nod, not rhetoric, and so built lasting deeds.

Fu Yue was revealed in a dream at Fuyan; Lü Wang's omen stirred on the banks of the Wei; Ning Qi's song rang out at the crossroads; and Zhang Liang received the book at the bridge at Xiapi. All awaited their appointed time and communed in spirit, relying on more than words; thus they could devise certain strategies and achieve immeasurable merit.

漢良受書於邳沂 refers to Zhang Liang receiving the book from the old man at the bridge at Xiapi; 沂 is glossed as a water bank and is not a second place named Yi. The worker correctly rejected 'at dawn' but misread 邳沂 as a place-name pair.

Think of Yi and Shu on Shouyang, Hui in a low post, Yan with his single meal, Confucius closing the Spring and Autumn at the western hunt—their names shook heaven and earth; they are our true exemplars.

Then there were Boyi, who upheld his conduct on Mount Shouyang; Liuxia Hui, who humbled his aspirations to take a dishonorable post; Yan Hui, who delighted in his basket of rice and gourd of water; and Confucius, who brought his classic to an end with the hunt in the west. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are truly exemplars for men such as us.

夷 is an abbreviated reference to Boyi, not an individual named Yi, while the source names no separate Shuqi here. The worker removed the invented second person but left the remaining allusions too cryptic for English readers.

Or again there were those who set pure conduct on Shouyang, Hui who lowered his will to a humbling office, Yan who took joy in a single basket and gourd, Confucius who finished his classic at the western hunt—their fame filled the gulf between Heaven and abyss; they are true models for our kind.

Or again, Boyi upheld his conduct on Shouyang; Liuxia Hui lowered his aspirations to accept a humiliating post; Yan Hui delighted in a basket of rice and a gourd of water; and Confucius ended his classic with the western hunt. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are true models for men such as us.
The Chinese explicitly names 夷, an abbreviation for Boyi. The prior literal omitted him, while the worker's bare 'Yi' failed to identify the allusion and left the other abbreviated names opaque.
Bian Que and Hua Tuo wield the needle with spirit, while Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang calculate gain across the boundless market.
Yi He and Bian Que mastered the needle and stone probe; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang's financial calculations knew no bounds.

龢、鵲 are Yi He and Bian Que, while 研、桑 are Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang. The worker correctly rejected Hua Tuo, Yi Dun, and Zhuo Sang, but its one-syllable labels were not useful identifications in English.
Bian Que and Hua Tuo bring essence to needle and stone, Yi Dun and Zhuo Sang reckon profit in the boundless.
Yi He and Bian Que brought their finest skill to needles and stone probes; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang applied mental calculation without limit.
The same abbreviations identify Yi He, Bian Que, Ji Yan, and Sang Hongyang. Expanding the names avoids replacing one set of misleading names with four ambiguous syllables.
